The boginka is a swamp fairy with a terrifying appearance—green-skinned with glowing eyes and long clawed fingers. The nożnica (night hag) appears as an old, bent woman who sits on sleepers' chests causing nightmares. The świtezianka is a lake-dwelling maiden of heartbreaking beauty who lures young men to their doom. The południca (noon witch) appears as a young woman in white who haunts fields at midday.

Boginki steal unborn children from mothers and replace them with their own sickly offspring. The południca appears to those who work in the fields at noon, the holiest hour, striking them with heatstroke or madness. The świtezianka tests the fidelity of lovers from the lake's shore. Dziwożony protect wild forests and animals, helping hunters who show respect but cursing those who overhunt. Protective charms include blessed herbs such as wormwood and St. John's wort, salt thrown over the shoulder, and iron nails carried in pockets. Sunday church bells and the sign of the cross are powerful against all Polish fairy spirits.
